text:
Choose Monzo if you want the best app experience, automated budgeting, and fee-free spending abroad. Choose Nationwide if you want branch access, member-only savings rates, a £50 interest-free overdraft buffer, and switching/loyalty bonuses.   
Referral Plug
+ 1

Because both offer free standard accounts and FSCS protection up to £120,000, your choice comes down to how you prefer to manage your money day-to-day.

Side-by-Side Comparison (Free Accounts)
Feature	Monzo (Free)	Nationwide (FlexAccount / FlexDirect)
App & Budgeting	Market-leading. Instant notifications, automatic spending categories, Salary Sorter, and ring-fenced Pots for bills.	Functional, basic. Clean interface for transfers and balances, though it lacks automated budgeting pots.
Branches & Cash	App-only. Cash deposits cost £1 per deposit at PayPoint or the Post Office. Cheques can be scanned in-app.	600+ UK branches. Free cash and cheque deposits in-branch, plus a pledge to keep branches open until at least 2030.
Spending Abroad	Fee-free card spending worldwide at the Mastercard rate. Free ATM withdrawals up to £400/30 days in the EEA (£200 outside).	2.99% non-sterling transaction fee on card payments and ATM withdrawals (waived only on paid FlexPlus).
Interest & Perks	0% on main balance; 2.80% AER (variable) in Instant Access Savings Pots.	FlexDirect: 5% AER on balances up to £1,500 + up to £10/month cashback for 12 months (requires £1,000/month pay-in), dropping to 1% AER after year one.
Bonuses	Occasional referral bonuses (£5–£50).	£175 switch bonus (via Current Account Switch Service) plus eligibility for annual £100 Fairer Share profit-share payouts (if you also hold a qualifying savings account or mortgage).
Overdraft	No free buffer. Arranged overdrafts charged at 19%, 29%, or 39% EAR depending on credit score.	£50 interest-free buffer on arranged overdrafts, then 39.9% EAR.
Paid Tiers (If You Want Packaged Extras)

Monzo Perks (£9/month): Boosts Instant Access savings to 3.55% AER and includes an annual Railcard, weekly Greggs treat, monthly Vue cinema ticket, Uber One, and YouTube Premium Lite.   
Monzo

Monzo Max (£19/month) vs. Nationwide FlexPlus (£18/month): Both bundle worldwide travel insurance, mobile phone insurance, and UK/European breakdown cover. FlexPlus covers your whole family by default and removes Nationwide's foreign card fees, whereas Monzo Max charges an extra £4/month for family cover (though it includes the Monzo Perks lifestyle freebies).   
PocketWise
+ 1

How to Decide

Go with Monzo if your salary arrives digitally, you rarely handle physical cash, you travel abroad, or you want visual pots to separate bill money from spending money automatically.   
Referral Plug

Go with Nationwide if you want the reassurance of local branches, plan to build a house deposit (unlocking member-only savings and mortgage deals), or want to claim the £175 switch bonus and potential annual Fairer Share payments.

The popular UK hybrid setup: Many people use Nationwide as their "hub" account (receiving their salary, holding Direct Debits, qualifying for Fairer Share, and keeping branch access) and transfer a weekly or monthly spending allowance to Monzo for day-to-day budgeting and holiday spending.

Do you value branch access and savings perks more, or are you primarily looking for day-to-day budgeting tools and travel-free spending?
